question.value: Can the dust over-density and kinematics of the circumbinary disc around the Class I binary L1551 IRS 5 be explained by the periodic perturbation of the inner binary, and is the over-density a long-lived dust concentration?

evidence.quote: provide evidence that the most prominent CBD features (disc size, morphology, kinematics) can be well explained by the periodic perturbation of the inner binary.
Hence, it is important to distinguish between persistent pressure maxima (causing dust traffic jams) and transient circumbinary structures.
This Letter makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.01205.L (PI: S. Yamamoto).

referee_caveats_inferred: Model-observation comparison is visual only, with no quantitative metric, residuals or uncertainty on the orbit choice.
Orbit is selected by resemblance among astrometrically allowed orbits, so the evidence for binary-driven origin is partly circular.
A single dust grain size (0.1 mm) and no grain growth or envelope limit the dust conclusions.
Different distances (146.4 pc versus 141 pc) are used in observations and in the radiative transfer model.
Self-calibration and clean details are not given, so the north/south flux ratio of 1.2 +/- 0.2 is hard to reproduce exactly.
